capabilities.businessOutcome: A member answers voluntarily after a recorded consent that can be withdrawn, each answer is held in a table built for it, linked to the member only where the union has decided it must be and readable by no one but the office the union names, published counts are aggregates that suppress groups below a decided minimum size, a snapshot is computed from consented answers and retained for the decided period, and every change commits with its audit record.
capabilities.gap: No capability named equity before Gate 0B.7, and UE-OMIT-PRIVACY-RIGHTS (receiving and fulfilling access, correction and portability requests) does not own a collection and monitoring programme. The three equity routes are the generic CRUD factory over member_segments, the saved member-search table: no self-identification, consent, monitoring or snapshot table exists in the application schema, equity_snapshots is declared only in the financial-service schema and revoked from the application roles, and the form and dashboard components that call the routes are mounted by no page. The form shows a consent text promising encryption, aggregate-only reporting with a ten-member minimum, deletion at any time and seven-year retention, none of which any source implements; the consent flag is a literal in the client body; the write floor is steward, so the member the form is for receives 403; the insert needs a name and filters the form never sends; and the reads return every saved segment, private ones included, to any member. This record closes none of them and names no data steward, reader, minimum group size or retention rule, which no source states.

The source has a federations table and a federation_remittances table, but the affiliates, dashboard, meetings and remittances paths are copies of the federation item route that return the one federation row of the session organization, the grievance benchmark path is a copy of the grievance collection route that the governance table refuses, and the locals paths serve bargaining_units rather than local unions.
